shipSystems.description: Every ship in SFB has a Ship System Display (SSD) — a schematic diagram showing all the ship's systems, shields, weapons, and hull structure. Each class has an individualized SSD.

ssdComponents.description: The SSD consists of check-off boxes for all the ship's structure and systems, arranged in the general layout of the ship.

sections.name: Shield Boxes
sections.description: Boxes around the ship's outline representing shield strength in each of the 6 directions. Marked out when damaged.

sections.name: Warp Engines
sections.description: Left and right warp engine boxes. Each box provides 1 unit of energy. Marked out when damaged, reducing energy output.

sections.name: Impulse Engines
sections.description: Left and right impulse engine boxes. Provide additional energy and sublight movement capability.

sections.name: Weapon Banks
sections.description: Individual weapon systems (phasers, disruptors, torpedo launchers, etc.). Marked out when destroyed.

sections.name: Control Spaces
sections.description: Main bridge and control system boxes. Loss of all control spaces cripples the ship.
sections.effect: Ship is crippled when all control spaces are destroyed.

sections.name: Damage Control Track
sections.description: Track showing the ship's damage control capability. The highest undestroyed box determines the current DamCon rating.
sections.effect: DamCon rating = shield points repaired per turn.

sections.name: Hull / Excess Damage Track
sections.description: Track for excess damage after systems are destroyed. When full, the ship is destroyed.

sections.name: Special Systems
sections.description: Boxes for special equipment like batteries, capacitors, cloaking devices, tractor beams, transporters, and labs.

sections.name: Ammunition Tracks
sections.description: Tracks for limited-use weapons like drones, shuttles, and probes. Marked off as they are used.

sections.name: Weapons Fire Charts
sections.description: Firing charts for all weapons on the ship, showing hit probabilities and damage by range band.

sections.name: Firing Arcs
sections.description: Diagram showing the firing arcs for each weapon bank.

sections.name: Miscellaneous Data
sections.description: Ship data including size class, point value, command rating, breakdown rating, and other reference information.

shipTypes.description: Ships are classified by type and role. The numbering system indicates the class and variant.

classes.description: The backbone of most fleets. The game was originally based on heavy cruisers.
Smaller, faster cruisers with lighter armament.
Wartime construction cruisers — relatively inexpensive substitutes for heavy cruisers.
Large, powerful ships with heavy armament and armor.
Superheavy ships. Only the Klingons historically built the B10.
classes.note: Other races have conjectural battleship designs in Module R5.

classes.description: Small, fast ships designed for reconnaissance.
Support ships with strong tractor beams for towing damaged vessels.
Ships that carry and launch fighters, interceptors, and shuttles.
Small sublight vessels used for patrol and light combat.
Fast sublight fighters designed to intercept seeking weapons.
Small transport vessels. Can be used for boarding, evacuation, or as decoys (Wild Weasels).

sizeClass.description: Ships are assigned a Size Class (SC) number that affects various game mechanics.

classes.description: Very large ships — heavy cruisers and large carriers.
Medium ships — light cruisers and war cruisers.
Small ships — scouts and patrol fighters.

pointValue.description: Each ship has a Basic Point Value (BPV) used for balanced game setup. Players agree on a point limit and build their fleets accordingly.
pointValue.usage: BPV ensures balanced matchups. All players must agree on entry conditions and ground rules.

ssdBookEvolution.description: SSDs have evolved over the editions of SFB.

history.description: Half-sheet diagrams. Some ship classes shared sheets with shaded boxes to differentiate variants.
Full-sheet Commander's SSDs with extra record-keeping information, firing charts, and ammo tracks.
Nine Commander's SSD Books produced, presenting new-style SSDs and new ship classes.
